title: Cross-mode Canary Orchestration Safety Matrix
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
When promoting model versions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments we lack a concise, automated policy surface that encodes environment-specific constraints (networking, KMS, auditability, capacity) while preserving consistent canary/A-B/shadow semantics and safe auto-rollback. The result: ad-hoc rollouts, surprising behavior in Private deployments (no external callbacks, stricter firewalling), and manual intervention to reconcile config parity before promotion.

Goal:
Produce a safety matrix and orchestration implementation patterns that: 1) express canonical canary/A-B/shadow policies at the API level; 2) map those policies to environment-specific execution plans (Hosted, Dedicated, Private); 3) implement deterministic auto-rollback triggers and guarded promotion gates; 4) surface actionable diagnostics and audit trails in Console for post-mortems.

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: rollout policy schema, environment policy mapping, auto-rollback heuristics, control-plane checks, observability hooks, gating UX signals for Console.
- Out-of-scope: full autoscaler algorithm changes, model training lifecycle, customer-specific legal/contract changes.

Key constraints by environment:
- Hosted: fastest feedback loop, richer control-plane telemetry, external health-check webhooks allowed, can perform rapid weight shifts.
- Dedicated: isolated GPU pools; capacity limits can cause slower ramp-ups; must respect tenant quotas and reserved-capacity contracts.
- Private: restricted outbound access, customer-managed KMS/HSM, limited control-plane visibility, and often batched upgrade windows (change windows). Many Private deployments cannot accept incoming health webhooks from our hosted control plane.

Design proposal (summary):
1) Canonical rollout policy schema (policy v1): JSON schema encoding phases (shadow -> canary -> ramp -> promote), failure windows, target weights, minimum sample counts, and required signals (latency p95, error-rate, model-quality drift from eval set). Schema links: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Canary+Policy+Schema+v1
2) Environment adapters: a deterministic translator that compiles policy v1 into per-environment plans. Each adapter adds constraints and operational transforms:
   - Hosted adapter: enable live traffic shaping, external callback probes, and short rollback windows (1-5m).
   - Dedicated adapter: validate reserved-capacity headroom, add rate-limited ramps, and schedule optional warmup traffic to pre-warm KV caches.
   - Private adapter: convert webhook-based probes into pull-based health checks via agent or sidecar, extend rollback windows to account for telemetry lag, and include config packaging for KMS references.
3) Safety matrix: a tabular mapping of policy fields to allowed ranges per environment (e.g., max initial canary weight 5% for Dedicated, 1% for Private unless authorized). This will be embedded in the control plane and used by a preflight validator.
4) Auto-rollback engine: rule-based system with pluggable signal evaluators. Default triggers: sustained error-rate > 0.5% for 5m OR latency p95 degradation > 2x baseline for 3m OR model-quality regression > 3% on canary eval suite. Rollback actions: immediate traffic shift to previous stable model + create incident + annotation in audit log.
5) Auditability & Console UX: every compiled plan and executed phase must be stored (immutable) with links to telemetry snapshots, the gating decisions, and the diffed config (KMS references redacted). Console should show: active canaries, estimated cost delta, and a one-click rollback with incident template.

Acceptance criteria:
- A policy v1 JSON schema is published to Confluence and validated by the preflight validator (link in PR).
- Environment adapters implemented for Hosted and Dedicated; Private adapter provides a deployable agent + docs for customer ops.
- Preflight validator rejects policy proposals that violate the safety matrix and surfaces clear remediation messages.
- Auto-rollback engine prototype detects two test failure modes in staging and issues rollback automatically (recorded in audit log).
- Console shows per-canary diagnostics and rollback button; rollout history is queryable via the API.

Implementation notes and decisions to date:
- We will use the existing rollout recorder (runtime-1.18) as the immutable store for compiled plans; this avoids building a new storage service but requires adding new attributes.
- Private adapter will ship as a small Go agent (listener+uploader) that can operate over customer-approved egress; avoid inbound webhooks.
- For auto-rollback signals, we will start with metrics we already collect in Console (error-rate, latency) and add a light-weight model-quality evaluation runner that executes a limited eval set against the canary for drift detection.
- We decided NOT to allow arbitrary weight jumps in Private by default; customers can opt-in with a signed change request.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Private telemetry lag causes false rollbacks. Mitigation: longer evaluation windows, hysteresis, and support for manual 'hold' state.
- Risk: Dedicated capacity exhaustion during warmup. Mitigation: preflight capacity check and optional warmup token budget.
- Risk: KMS/HSM references leak. Mitigation: redact secrets in audit logs and require KMS reference validation preflight.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Cross-Mode+Canary+Orchestration
- Design doc draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Canary+Policy+Schema+v1
- Staging test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/staging-canaries
- Implementation PR (adapter skeleton): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1284

Next steps / plan for this cycle:
- Implement preflight validator rules (2 days)
- Deliver Hosted + Dedicated adapters MVP (5 days)
- Submit Private agent design and test harness (3 days)
- Run staged experiments on canary flows and validate auto-rollback triggers (4 days)

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to the safety matrix values for initial canary weights and evaluation sample sizes; these are conservative by design but can be tuned after live experiments.
- The Private adapter architecture assumes a minimal agent; if Security desires an inbound proxy instead, we need to revisit design and timeline.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Policy v1 JSON schema published and linked from ticket.
2) Preflight validator enforces safety matrix and emits human-friendly messages.
3) Hosted and Dedicated adapters compile policy v1 to executable plans and run at least one staged canary in staging.
4) Private adapter design doc + agent prototype available for customer ops review.
5) Auto-rollback engine triggers on two synthetic failure scenarios in staging and records rollback event in audit log.
6) Console displays canary status, telemetry snapshot, and rollback control for the staged runs.
